<reason>B won a close, high-quality debate by making the hard case decide: in one-party counties the firewall is structurally paper, so capture risk is largest where a watchdog is most needed. A stayed closer to the motion’s with-vs-without comparison and landed a vivid vacuum/shared-object story, but abandoned the trust mechanism and never named a barrier that survives one-party appointment, renewal, and self-censorship. B’s comparative weighing—contested public desks as a new culture-war front, plus a captured desk occupying the vacuum—gave the cleaner reason the net fails.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s answer that one county desk can polarize the out-group and certify innocence for the in-group, so A’s “distrusted yet legitimating” contradiction is how capture actually works—not a fatal inconsistency.</best_rebuttal>
